concern_details.detail: main components in the booking process, their responsibilities, interactions and dependencies
concern_details.why: All components on the makeReservation path are shown with responsibilities in inventory.json and connected through provided/required interfaces; the dependency chain web/swing -> facade -> resMgr -> strategy/domain/registry -> persist -> db matches the code.
REST controller and Swing wizard both call LibraryFacade.makeReservation, which delegates to ReservationManager.makeReservation (LibraryFacade.java:117-118).
ReservationManager calls Area.getAvailableSeats, which uses Seat.isAvailable and the registries (Area.java:49-57, Seat.java:44-52); the view shows resMgr ..> IDomain and domain ..> IRegistry.

Validation and the one-reservation-per-slot rule live in ReservationManager (ReservationManager.java:65-155), seat choice in the strategy, duplicate check in Student; the view names these and the README points where new rules go.

concern_details.detail: which components manage and store reservations
concern_details.why: createAndSave builds the reservation and saves it through ReservationRegistry (ReservationManager.java:125-139), which uses PersistenceManager over MySQL; all on the diagram.

concern_details.detail: which components interact with external services such as notifications
concern_details.why: The notification components are present, but the provider/consumer of the Notification service interface is inverted in the view (Notification manager drawn as provider, Email adapter as user), so the connection to the external email service is shown wrongly; the external gateway itself is only a hidden member of the adapter.

concern_details.detail: which parts need to be modified and which other components may be affected
concern_details.why: Dependency arrows let the reader trace who depends on Reservation manager and the domain model; the guidance on where to add rules is in the README/inventory rather than the diagram. The notification dependency on domain states (messageForState) is omitted from the diagram, so impact on Notification manager is not visible from the view itself.

level_why: Twelve components at the granularity of manager/subsystem with named interfaces fit a balanced level for a developer: each rule-bearing unit (manager, strategy, domain model) is visible without descending into classes or DTOs, and unrelated managers are left out.

findings.claim: The view shows Notification manager providing the Notification service interface; in the code NotificationManager is the consumer: it holds a NotificationService field and calls it to send. The interface is implemented by NotificationServiceAdapter.
findings.fix: Make notifMgr require INotifySvc (notifMgr ..> INotifySvc : <<use>>) instead of providing it.

findings.claim: The view shows the Email notification adapter using the Notification service interface; in the code the adapter implements (provides) it, so the dependency direction toward the external service is reversed and the diagram's meaning changes.
findings.fix: Draw mailAdapter - INotifySvc as the provided interface (lollipop) and remove the <<use>> dependency from mailAdapter.

findings.claim: The external email gateway (the external service the concern explicitly mentions) is folded into the adapter, so the boundary to the external service is not visible.
findings.fix: Optionally show the Email gateway as an external component (e.g. <<external>>) used by the Email notification adapter.

findings.claim: The Student actor is drawn as directly using the Library facade API; the student reaches the facade only through the REST boundary or the Swing wizard.
findings.fix: Connect the Student actor to the REST boundary and Swing booking wizard instead of to IFacade.

findings.claim: Notification manager depends on the domain model (reservation state enum, Student) and on the registry (getEndingReservations, update); these dependencies are omitted, so a developer changing reservation states would not see that Notification manager is affected from the diagram alone.
findings.fix: Add notifMgr ..> IDomain and notifMgr ..> IRegistry, or note the dependency on the diagram.

findings.claim: <<entity>> is a class-level stereotype; on a component that groups entity classes and states it is non-standard.
findings.fix: Drop the stereotype or use a component-level one such as <<subsystem>>.

findings.claim: The alias suggests an implementation and the interface is drawn as required by Reservation manager only, whereas it is the domain's Reservation (subject) that calls Observer.update; Reservation manager only attaches the observer.
findings.fix: Optionally add domain ..> IObserverImpl and keep resMgr's use as the attachment step.
